correctness.rationale: Normalize the leading sign first; the all-positive sign sector and its simultaneous negative copy have total sign probability 1/16. In magnitudes the last nontrivial Hurwitz minor gives B₂>u B₄+u⁻¹ B₀ with u=B₁/B₃, and implies the preceding minor. The folded-Cauchy u is independent of the three remaining magnitudes. The Gaussian cone (G₄>0,G₀>0,G₂−uG₄−u⁻¹G₀>0) already forces G₂>0, so its probability must be multiplied by eight. The trivariate sign expansion yields the two negative arcsines with correlations −u/s, −1/(us), s²=1+u²+u⁻². Inversion of u exchanges them and preserves the Cauchy measure; u=tan θ gives the stated compact integral and its exact coefficient. Leading coefficient, zero roots, and nonzero imaginary roots occur on null sets: for the latter, assuming A₃≠0 requires t²=A₁/A₃ and the quartic Hurwitz determinant to vanish. Independently, odd index occurs iff the product of roots A₀/A₄ is negative; complex pairs have positive product, so each odd index has mass 1/4 by the P(−z) symmetry. The cited Corollary 5.2/Lemma 3.1(c) also establishes that relation. A fresh 65-digit mpmath integration on [0,1,∞] of atan(u²/√(1+u²))/(1+u²) gave h=0.00928384472429811895714992419655543453132463760732168417153218…; this is not an interval certificate.
